newsitem.title: CONGO: Lull as Brazzaville awaits word from mediators.
newsitem.headline: Lull as Brazzaville awaits word from mediators.

text.p: The battered capital of the Congo Republic enjoyed relative calm on Saturday after a much-flouted truce was extended, mediators and witnesses said.
A spokesman for Brazzaville mayor and mediator Bernard Kolelas said a national mediation committee expected to make an announcement later in the day on progress so far.
"Every time we say the ceasefire is being respected, there's the odd bit of firing," the spokesman said. "But overall, everything is quiet."
A month-old showdown between President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso has killed hundreds of people and put tens of thousands of civilians to flight.
The latest truce, proposed by international mediator President Omar Bongo of Gabon, took effect from midnight (2300 GMT) Friday. Past truces have collapsed after a day or so.
Kolelas, whose own supporters were at the heart of similar bloody ethnic and political clashes after a disputed 1993 parliamentary election, had talks with both men this week.
Lissouba on Tuesday accepted a nine-point blueprint proposed by Kolelas's committee as a basis for negotiation. Sassou has yet to make public his response.
Friday saw scattered shooting but witnesses said soldiers or fighters appeared to be firing for the sake of it.
The showdown began on June 5 when troops surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militias ahead of a presidential election that had been planned for July 27.
